title: Coast Guard Station Hatteras Inlet provides water safety tips
description: Petty Officer 1st Class Lane Parker and Petty Officer 2nd Class Pete Coia, both boatswain's mates assigned to U.S. Coast Guard Station Hatteras Inlet, provide water safety tips June 24, 2026, in Hatteras, North Carolina. Station Hatteras is a small boat station in the Outer Banks with primary missions of search and rescue, law enforcement and marine environmental protection. (U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 3rd Class Christine Bills)
keywords: Hatteras, safety, North Carolina, USCG, East District

transcript.text: I'm , BM1 Lane Parker with Coast Guard
Station Hatteras Inlet . I'm a coxswain
on the motor lifeboat here . I'm BM 2
Pete Coya . I'm a surfman here at
Station Hatteras Inlet . Oftentimes we
are just looking for a head bobbing in
the water , so bright colored PFDs ,
visual or audio distress signals ,
whistle , horn , flares , mirror ,
lights , all those sorts of things help
us out immensely when trying to spot
someone who's floating in the water by
themselves . I would say one of the
most important things is just
understanding the forecast and the
weather conditions prior to going out
in addition to understanding your
comfortability level of being on the
water and putting yourself in that
position and , and understanding the
consequences of not being comfortable
or not taking the appropriate
preventative actions to ensure that if
you end up in a distress situation you
have the appropriate means to signal
distress or notify the Coast Guard .
